question: Does the mere presence of consciousness in a knower make objects knowable?
premises: A cloth does not acquire the pot's broad-base form merely because that form exists elsewhere.
Consciousness may be present and inhere in the knower.
A property not belonging to an object's nature cannot be transferred to it by mere presence of something else.
inference: Even when consciousness inheres in the knower, entities do not become knowable if knowability were an external property.
plain_english: A cloth does not become broad-based just because a pot is. In the same way, even if consciousness is present and belongs to the knower, entities would not become knowable if knowability were something external to them.
